senses-order.title: Hearing, Then Sight
senses-order.hook: The Quran lists hearing before sight, the order in which the senses awaken before birth.
senses-order.science.0: The inner ear is working by about 18–20 weeks of pregnancy, and the fetus first responds to sound around week 19 (Hepper & Shahidullah, 1994). The eyelids fuse shut at about 10 weeks and reopen only around 26 weeks.
senses-order.science.1: After birth, newborns already recognise their mother's voice (DeCasper & Fifer, 1980): the sound they heard in the womb.
senses-order.science.2: The Quran lists “hearing” before “sight” in almost every place the two occur, and in 32:9 adds “hearts”, the seat of understanding, third.
senses-order.stats.0.label: First fetal responses to sound
senses-order.stats.1.label: Eyelids reopen
senses-order.proof.0.title: DeCasper and Fifer: newborns know the voice
senses-order.proof.0.text: Newborns suck faster to hear their mother's voice than another woman's: they learned it in the womb.
senses-order.proof.1.title: Hepper and Shahidullah: sound at 19 weeks
senses-order.proof.1.text: Ultrasound shows fetuses moving in response to sound from 19 weeks of pregnancy.
senses-order.proof.2.title: The eyes open later
senses-order.proof.2.text: The eyelids fuse shut around week 10 and reopen around week 26, and the retina responds to light later still.
senses-order.fit.0: Hearing is listed before sight in 32:9, 76:2 and other verses.
senses-order.fit.1: Fetal hearing works weeks before the eyes open.
senses-order.gap.0: The Arabic wa (“and”) does not set an order.
senses-order.gap.1: Hearing before sight may simply be the usual order in which the Quran lists them.
senses-order.gap.2: “Hearts”, listed third in 32:9, are the first organ to work in the embryo, so the list is not a developmental timeline.
senses-order.media.0.cap: A human embryo at about 8 weeks, before the senses have begun to work.
fingerprints.title: The Fingertips
fingerprints.hook: God is able to reassemble the bones, “down to the very tips of the fingers.”
fingerprints.science.0: Fingerprint ridges form in the womb between weeks 10 and 17 and stay the same for life. They differ between individuals, even identical twins.
fingerprints.science.1: Francis Galton's 1892 book “Finger Prints” established scientifically that they are permanent and unique, which opened the door to forensic identification. Before that, fingerprints were pressed into clay and used as personal marks in ancient Babylon and China.
fingerprints.science.2: The verse, in the context of resurrection, says God is able to put together even the banān, the fingertips: the finest and most individual detail of a person.
fingerprints.stats.0.label: When the fingerprint pattern forms
fingerprints.stats.1.label: Galton proves permanence and uniqueness
fingerprints.proof.0.title: Grew: the ridges
fingerprints.proof.0.text: Nehemiah Grew describes the ridges and pores on fingers and palms.
fingerprints.proof.1.title: Mayer: no two alike
fingerprints.proof.1.text: Johann Mayer states that no two people's fingerprint patterns are exactly alike.
fingerprints.proof.2.title: Purkinje: nine patterns
fingerprints.proof.2.text: Jan Purkinje sorts fingerprints into nine pattern types.
fingerprints.proof.3.title: Galton: permanent and unique
fingerprints.proof.3.text: Francis Galton shows that fingerprints stay the same through life and are distinctive enough to identify people. The same year, Juan Vucetich in Argentina uses a bloody fingerprint to solve a murder.
fingerprints.proof.4.title: Twins
fingerprints.proof.4.text: Studies of identical twins find their fingerprints are similar but different.
fingerprints.fit.0: Banān (fingertips) names the part of the body whose ridges identify each person.
fingerprints.fit.1: The verse stresses God's power to shape even the finest detail.
fingerprints.gap.0: The context is resurrection, not identification.
fingerprints.gap.1: Banān can mean fingers or fingertips generally.
fingerprints.gap.2: Fingerprints were pressed into clay as marks in ancient Babylon and China, so their individuality was not hidden.
fingerprints.gap.3: Science has not proved that no two prints are identical, only that none has been found.
fingerprints.media.0.cap: A fingerprint: a plain whorl pattern.
fingerprints.media.1.cap: A fingerprint: a central pocket loop whorl.
moon-split.title: The Splitting of the Moon
moon-split.hook: “The Hour has come near, and the moon has split.” A sign in the Islamic tradition, not a scientific discovery.
moon-split.sciH: What we can and cannot say
moon-split.science.0: Muslim scholars have long held that this event happened at Makkah during the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, when the disbelievers demanded a sign: the Moon appeared split in two, with the mountain seen between the two parts. It is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari (for example 3636, 3637 and 4864) and in Sahih Muslim, from companions including Anas ibn Malik and Abdullah ibn Masʿud.
moon-split.science.1: This is a miracle in the Islamic tradition: an event given as a sign, not a natural process. Science studies repeatable natural processes, so it can neither prove nor disprove it, and this app does not claim otherwise.
moon-split.science.2: You may have seen posts claiming that “NASA found a crack across the Moon” that proves it. No NASA statement supports that. The long channels seen on the Moon are lunar rilles, ordinary features made by ancient lava flows and faulting. We do not use that story.
moon-split.proof.0.title: The reports
moon-split.proof.0.text: Several companions, including Abdullah ibn Masʿud and Anas ibn Malik, narrate that the Moon appeared split in two at Makkah.
moon-split.proof.1.title: The collections
moon-split.proof.1.text: Al-Bukhari (d. 870) and Muslim (d. 875) record the reports in their Sahih collections, which Muslim scholars grade as authentic.
moon-split.proof.2.title: What the Moon's channels really are
moon-split.proof.2.text: Apollo and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographs show that the Moon's long channels (rilles) are old lava channels and fault valleys. They are not a split and are unrelated to this event.
moon-split.proof.2.cap: Hadley Rille, a lunar lava channel (Apollo 15).
moon-split.fit.0: Verse 54:1 states the event in the past tense right after “the Hour has drawn near”.
moon-split.fit.1: 54:2 says that when they see a sign they turn away and call it magic. Classical commentaries connect this to the Makkans calling it sorcery.
moon-split.gap.0: No physical test is possible: it is a reported miracle, accepted on the strength of transmission.
moon-split.gap.1: A minority of scholars read inshaqqa as a future sign of the Last Hour.
moon-split.gap.2: Historians do not generally accept any independent record outside the Muslim sources.
moon-split.gap.3: Claims that NASA photographed the split are false.
moon-split.media.1.cap: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter: a tour of the Moon's surface.
roman-prophecy.title: The Romans Will Win
roman-prophecy.hook: A prophecy about a superpower war: the defeated Romans (ar-Rūm, the Byzantines) “will overcome”, within “three to nine years”.
roman-prophecy.science.0: In 614 CE Sasanian Persian armies took Jerusalem from the Byzantine (Roman) Empire, and by 619 they had conquered Egypt. The Byzantines seemed finished. In Makkah the small, persecuted Muslim community sympathised with the Christian Romans against the Persians.
roman-prophecy.science.1: From 622 Emperor Heraclius launched a counter-offensive. At the decisive Battle of Nineveh in 627 the Persian army was crushed, and by 628 the war was over: the reversal the verses foretold.
roman-prophecy.science.2: “Adnā al-arḍ” can mean “the nearest land” or “the lowest land”. The Dead Sea region, the lowest exposed land on Earth (about 430 m below sea level), lay in the war zone.
roman-prophecy.stats.0.label: Persians take Jerusalem
roman-prophecy.stats.1.label: Byzantines win at Nineveh
roman-prophecy.stats.2.label: What biḍʿ means in Arabic
roman-prophecy.proof.0.title: Jerusalem falls
roman-prophecy.proof.0.text: Persian armies capture Jerusalem. The Armenian historian Sebeos and the Greek Antiochus Strategos record the massacre and the loss of the True Cross.
roman-prophecy.proof.1.title: Egypt is lost
roman-prophecy.proof.1.text: The Persians finish conquering Egypt, the granary of the Byzantine Empire.
roman-prophecy.proof.2.title: Heraclius strikes back
roman-prophecy.proof.2.text: Emperor Heraclius counter-attacks through Anatolia and Armenia, as the chroniclers Theophanes and the Paschal Chronicle record. In December 627 he wins at Nineveh.
roman-prophecy.proof.2.cap: The Sasanian Empire at its height, about 621 CE.
roman-prophecy.proof.3.title: Peace and the Cross
roman-prophecy.proof.3.text: The Persian king Khosrow II is overthrown and peace is made. Heraclius returns the True Cross to Jerusalem in 630.
roman-prophecy.fit.0: The Romans lose badly and then win: the war reversed within about 14 years of the fall of Jerusalem.
roman-prophecy.fit.1: The verse places the defeat “in the nearest land”, and the Dead Sea region saw fighting.
roman-prophecy.fit.2: Biḍʿ means 3 to 9 years, and the Byzantine recovery began within that window (622–625).
roman-prophecy.gap.0: The date of revelation and the start of the count of years are debated.
roman-prophecy.gap.1: The final victory (627–628) came 13–14 years after 614, longer than nine years; the defence counts from the start of the recovery.
roman-prophecy.gap.2: The story of the revelation comes from Islamic sources, although the war itself is history.
roman-prophecy.gap.3: Adnā al-arḍ has two readings: “nearest” or “lowest” land.
roman-prophecy.media.0.cap: The Sasanian Persian Empire at its greatest extent, about 621 CE.
roman-prophecy.media.1.cap: The Dead Sea, the lowest exposed land on Earth.
ant-valley.title: The Ant Who Warned Her Colony
ant-valley.hook: An ant says, “O ants, enter your homes”, and biologists have since shown that ants really do warn and call one another.
ant-valley.science.0: Ants live in colonies of thousands to millions and coordinate through chemicals, touch and sound. Alarm chemicals send nestmates rushing to shelter or to defend it, and trail chemicals mark the way to food.
ant-valley.science.1: The word “pheromone” was coined in 1959. In 1962 E. O. Wilson showed how fire ants lay a chemical trail from food to the nest. In 1965 Hubert Markl found that leaf-cutter ants trapped underground rub a ridge on their bodies to make sounds that call nestmates to dig them out.
ant-valley.science.2: Some ants build enormous nations: one supercolony of Argentine ants stretches about 6,000 km along the European coast, from Italy to Spain.
ant-valley.stats.0.label: The word “pheromone” is coined
ant-valley.stats.1.label: Fire-ant trail signals decoded (Wilson)
ant-valley.stats.2.label: Leaf-cutter ants found to call for help by sound
ant-valley.disc.who: Karlson & Lüscher · E. O. Wilson · Hubert Markl
ant-valley.proof.0.title: Pheromones get a name
ant-valley.proof.0.text: Peter Karlson and Martin Lüscher coin the word “pheromone” for chemical signals passed between members of one species, the same year Adolf Butenandt identifies the first one, bombykol, from silk moths.
ant-valley.proof.1.title: Wilson: the fire-ant trail
ant-valley.proof.1.text: E. O. Wilson shows that fire ants lay a chemical trail from food to the nest, and that nestmates follow it and reinforce it. He also studies how alarm chemicals send a colony into action.
ant-valley.proof.2.title: Markl: ants that call by sound
ant-valley.proof.2.text: Hubert Markl finds that leaf-cutter ants trapped underground rub a ridge on their bodies to make sounds that call nestmates to dig them out.
ant-valley.proof.3.title: The Ants
ant-valley.proof.3.text: Bert Hölldobler and E. O. Wilson publish The Ants, a 700-page account of ant societies, their communication and alarm signals. It wins a Pulitzer Prize in 1991.
ant-valley.proof.4.title: One colony, 6,000 kilometres long
ant-valley.proof.4.text: Argentine ants along the European coast, from Italy to Spain, are shown to belong to a single supercolony that recognises its own members (Giraud and colleagues).
ant-valley.fit.0: One ant warns the others to go into their homes: real ants give alarm signals that send nestmates to shelter or to defend it.
ant-valley.fit.1: The verse speaks of ants as a people (an-naml) with dwellings, matching colonies with nests and shared rules.
ant-valley.gap.0: The verse is part of a story in which Solomon understands the ant's words; it is not offered as a lesson in ant biology.
ant-valley.gap.1: Namlah is a grammatically feminine noun, so “she said” does not by itself show that the speaker was a worker.
ant-valley.gap.2: Ants do not speak in words: their signals are chemical, touch and sound.
ant-valley.media.1.cap: Leaf-cutter ants carrying leaf pieces along a trail.
ant-valley.media.2.cap: Leaf-cutter ants on the move in Trinidad.
bee-dance.title: The Bee's Paths Made Easy
bee-dance.hook: Told to “follow the ways of your Lord made easy”, a bee can fly kilometres and tell its sisters exactly where the flowers are, by dancing.
bee-dance.science.0: A forager that finds rich flowers returns to the hive and performs a waggle dance: a figure-of-eight run. The angle of the straight run, measured against the vertical comb, tells the direction of the flowers relative to the Sun, and its length tells the distance.
bee-dance.science.1: Karl von Frisch decoded the dance in the 1940s and shared the 1973 Nobel Prize for it. In 2005 harmonic radar tracked bees leaving the hive after watching a dance and showed that they really flew to the place the dance described.
bee-dance.science.2: Bees find their way by the Sun, by the pattern of polarised light in the sky and by landmarks, and can forage several kilometres from the hive.
bee-dance.stats.0.label: Nobel Prize for decoding the bee dance
bee-dance.stats.1.label: Radar shows bees really follow the dance
bee-dance.stats.2.label: A robot bee successfully recruits real foragers
bee-dance.disc.who: Karl von Frisch · Riley et al.
bee-dance.proof.0.title: Von Frisch decodes the dance
bee-dance.proof.0.text: Karl von Frisch trains marked bees to feeders at set distances and directions and watches their dances back at the hive, until he can read direction and distance from them. He publishes the result in 1946.
bee-dance.proof.1.title: Nobel Prize
bee-dance.proof.1.text: Von Frisch shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Konrad Lorenz and Nikolaas Tinbergen for discoveries about animal behaviour.
bee-dance.proof.2.title: A robot bee
bee-dance.proof.2.text: Axel Michelsen and colleagues build a mechanical dancing bee. Real foragers watch it and fly to the feeder it indicates.
bee-dance.proof.3.title: Radar tracks the recruits
bee-dance.proof.3.text: Using harmonic radar, Joseph Riley and colleagues follow individual bees leaving the hive after watching a dance and show that they fly to the place the dance described.
bee-dance.fit.0: “Paths” (subul) “made easy” (dhululan) matches flight paths that other bees can follow, described in the dance.
bee-dance.fit.1: The bee is “inspired” (awḥā), matching a largely inborn behaviour: bees can dance without being taught.
bee-dance.fit.2: The instruction to go out and eat from all the fruits matches foraging trips.
bee-dance.gap.0: The dance is not mentioned in the verse; linking “the ways of your Lord made easy” to it is a modern reading.
bee-dance.gap.1: Classical commentators read the ways as the paths back to the hive, or as the ways God has smoothed for the bee.
bee-dance.gap.2: Waḥy (inspiration) is a religious word; science calls the behaviour instinct and does not address it.
bee-dance.gap.3: Other honeybee species dance differently, and some bees do not dance at all.
bee-dance.media.0.cap: How the waggle dance encodes direction and distance.
bee-dance.media.1.cap: Bees on the comb: a dancer is surrounded by followers.
locust-swarm.title: Like Scattered Locusts
locust-swarm.hook: People rise “like locusts spread out”, and locust science shows how shy solitary insects become a swarm within hours.
locust-swarm.science.0: A swarm of desert locusts can hold 40 to 80 million adults per square kilometre. Each locust eats about its own weight in food a day, so one square kilometre of swarm eats what 35,000 people would in a day, and swarms can be carried up to about 150 km in a day on the wind.
locust-swarm.science.1: For a long time solitary grasshoppers and swarming locusts were thought to be different animals. In 1921 Boris Uvarov showed they are one species in two forms, called phases.
locust-swarm.science.2: In 2009 a team led by Michael Anstey and Stephen Simpson showed what flips the switch: crowding, especially the touch of other locusts on the hind legs, raises serotonin in the nervous system. Within about two hours a shy solitary insect becomes gregarious, and blocking serotonin stops the change.
locust-swarm.stats.0.label: Locusts per km² of swarm (FAO)
locust-swarm.stats.1.label: People whose daily food one km² of swarm eats
locust-swarm.stats.2.label: For a solitary locust to turn gregarious (2009)
locust-swarm.disc.who: Boris Uvarov · Michael Anstey & Stephen Simpson
locust-swarm.proof.0.title: Uvarov: one species, two forms
locust-swarm.proof.0.text: Boris Uvarov shows that solitary grasshoppers and swarming locusts are one species in two forms, which he calls phases.
locust-swarm.proof.1.title: Touch is the trigger
locust-swarm.proof.1.text: Stephen Simpson and colleagues show that a solitary desert locust turns gregarious when it is repeatedly touched on the hind legs, as it is in a crowd.
locust-swarm.proof.2.title: Serotonin flips the switch
locust-swarm.proof.2.text: Michael Anstey, Stephen Simpson and colleagues show that crowding raises serotonin in the locust's nervous system, and that blocking serotonin stops the change: within about two hours a shy insect becomes gregarious.
locust-swarm.proof.3.title: A modern upsurge
locust-swarm.proof.3.text: The worst desert-locust upsurge in decades hits East Africa, Yemen and South Asia. Satellites, ground surveys and aerial spraying, coordinated by the FAO, are used to track and counter it.
locust-swarm.fit.0: “Locusts spread out” pictures a huge crowd dispersing in all directions, just as a swarm looks.
locust-swarm.fit.1: 7:133 lists locusts among the plagues that strip the land, and a swarm does exactly that.
locust-swarm.gap.0: 54:7 is a simile about the Day of Judgment, not about locust biology.
locust-swarm.gap.1: The serotonin switch is a modern discovery; the verse says nothing about it.
locust-swarm.gap.2: Locust plagues were well known in the ancient Near East, so the picture was familiar.
locust-swarm.media.1.cap: Gregarious desert locust nymphs roosting together in Mauritania.
locust-swarm.media.2.cap: A locust in flight, filmed at high speed.
